cards.title: Minor burns
facts: Cooling a burn under cool running water for about 20 minutes limits the damage.
Ice, butter and toothpaste can trap heat or damage skin.
Burns to the face, hands, or large areas need medical help.
do: Cool the burn under cool (not icy) running water for about 20 minutes
Remove rings or tight items near the burn, unless stuck
Cover loosely with cling film or a clean, non-fluffy cloth
Tell an adult; get medical help for big burns or burns on face or hands
dont: No ice, butter, oil or toothpaste
Don't pop blisters
Don't use fluffy cotton wool

myths.statement: Putting toothpaste on a burn helps it heal faster.
myths.truth: Toothpaste can trap heat and irritate the skin. Cool it under running water for about 20 minutes.

myths.statement: Holding a small burn under cool running water is the right first step.
myths.truth: Cool water for about 20 minutes reduces pain and damage.

quiz.q: You touch a hot pan and burn your finger. What first?
quiz.explanation: Cool running water for about 20 minutes is the right first step.

situations: {At}, {name} accidentally touches the hot handle of a pressure cooker and burns their palm. {relation} says 'Quick, put toothpaste on it!'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Cool it under cool running water for about 20 minutes
No toothpaste, ice or butter
rubric.note: They can make the burn worse.

rubric.point: Cover loosely with a clean cloth or cling film
Tell an adult / get medical help if it's big
rubric.note: Hand burns can need a doctor.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Nosebleeds
facts: Leaning forward stops blood running down the throat.
Pinching the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes stops most nosebleeds.
do: Sit down and lean forward
Pinch the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes without letting go
Breathe through the mouth
Get medical help if it lasts more than 20 minutes or followed a head injury
dont: Don't tilt the head back
Don't lie down
Don't blow the nose right after

myths.statement: For a nosebleed, tilt your head back.
myths.truth: Lean forward instead, so blood doesn't run down your throat, and pinch the soft part of the nose.

quiz.q: Your friend has a nosebleed. How should they sit?
quiz.explanation: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes.

situations: During class {at}, {name}'s friend suddenly gets a nosebleed and looks scared. Someone shouts 'Tilt your head back!'
scenario.question: How should {name} help?

rubric.point: Sit up and lean forward (not back)
rubric.note: Leaning back makes blood run down the throat.

rubric.point: Pinch the soft part of the nose
rubric.note: Pinch just below the bony part for about 10 minutes.

rubric.point: Stay calm and tell a teacher
Get help if it doesn't stop in 20 minutes
rubric.note: Long or heavy bleeding needs a doctor.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke
facts: Heatstroke is an emergency: very hot body, confusion or fainting.
Thirst, headache, dizziness and heavy sweating are early warning signs.
do: Move the person to shade or a cool room
Loosen tight clothing
Give small sips of water if they're awake
Cool them with wet cloths and fanning
Call 112 if they are confused, faint or very hot
dont: Don't give fizzy or energy drinks
Don't leave them alone
Don't force water if they're drowsy

myths.statement: If you're not thirsty, you can't be getting dehydrated.
myths.truth: Thirst comes late. Drink regularly in hot weather and during sport.

quiz.q: A friend feels dizzy and sick after football in the sun. First step?
options: Move to shade and sip water
quiz.explanation: Cool down in the shade and sip water. Call for help if they get confused or faint.

situations: It's {time} {at}. After a long race in the sun, {name}'s teammate says they feel dizzy, has a headache and is very red in the face.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Move them to shade or a cool place
rubric.note: Get out of the heat first.

rubric.point: Give sips of water
Cool them down (wet cloth, loosen clothes)
Tell an adult / call 112 if confused or fainting

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Choking: what to do
facts: If someone can cough or speak, their airway is only partly blocked.
If they can't breathe, speak or cough, it is an emergency.
do: Encourage them to keep coughing if they can
If they can't breathe or speak, shout for an adult and call 112
Trained people give back blows and abdominal thrusts
dont: Don't put fingers blindly into their mouth
Don't give water to someone who is choking
Don't leave them alone

myths.statement: Giving water helps someone who is choking.
myths.truth: Water can make it worse. Encourage coughing; if they can't breathe, get help and call 112.

quiz.q: Your friend is choking but can still cough loudly. What do you do?
quiz.explanation: Strong coughing is the body's best way to clear the blockage. Stay with them.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Direct pressure first aid for severe cuts and bleeding
facts: Continuous firm pressure directly on an open cut stops over 90% of bleeding by enabling clotting.
Peeling off a blood-soaked bandage rips away developing platelet clots; always layer new cloth on top.
do: Press firmly on the wound using a clean cloth, sterile gauze, or clean handkerchief
Maintain continuous pressure for at least 10 minutes without lifting to check
Elevate the injured limb above heart level if no bone fracture is suspected
dont: Never put turmeric powder, mud, coffee or ash on open wounds
Never remove an embedded object like glass or metal

myths.statement: Applying turmeric or coffee powder to deep wounds heals them safely.
myths.truth: Home powders cause horrific wound infections and tissue necrosis. Use clean direct pressure.

quiz.q: A friend cuts their arm deeply on broken glass and blood is flowing. What is the immediate first aid?
options: Apply firm continuous direct pressure with a clean cloth
quiz.explanation: Firm direct pressure compresses severed capillaries and allows natural clotting.

situations: In the craft room at {at}, a cutter slips and {name}'s friend cuts their hand deeply.
scenario.question: What should {name} do right now?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Apply firm direct pressure with a clean cloth or gauze
rubric.note: Compresses blood vessels to stop bleeding.

rubric.point: If cloth soaks through, add another cloth on top without removing the first
rubric.keys: don'?t remove|layer on top|add more cloth

rubric.point: Call teacher/school nurse and seek medical help for stitches/tetanus

sources.name: Indian Red Cross Society First Aid Manual

cards.title: Dog bite and scratch: Urgent rabies protocol
facts: Rabies is transmitted via infected animal saliva and is nearly 100% fatal once symptoms appear.
Washing thoroughly with soap and running water physically washes away virus particles.
do: Wash wound immediately under running tap water with soap for at least 15 continuous minutes
Apply an antiseptic solution like povidone iodine after thorough washing
Visit a medical clinic the same day for anti-rabies vaccination (PEP) and tetanus toxoid
dont: Never apply chili powder, lime, oil, or turmeric to animal bites
Never tie a tight bandage over open animal bite wounds

myths.statement: A minor scratch from a friendly stray puppy does not need a doctor's visit.
myths.truth: Any scratch that breaks skin can transmit rabies. Immediate washing and vaccination are mandatory.

quiz.q: What is the first and most critical step immediately after a dog bite or scratch?
options: Wash under running water with soap for 15 minutes
quiz.explanation: Soap dissolves the rabies viral lipid envelope and running water flushes it away.

situations: While playing at {at}, a stray dog bites {name}'s calf, breaking the skin.
scenario.question: What must {name} do immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wash the wound under running tap water with soap for 15 minutes
rubric.note: Flushes out saliva and inactivates rabies virus.

rubric.point: Apply antiseptic and do not bandage tightly
rubric.note: Prevents secondary infection without trapping virus.

rubric.point: Go to a hospital or clinic on the same day for rabies vaccine

cards.title: Fainting first aid and the recovery position
facts: Fainting (syncope) occurs when temporary blood flow to the brain drops.
Laying the person flat and elevating their feet returns pooled blood to the heart and brain.
do: Lay the person flat on their back and elevate legs 30 cm (12 inches)
Loosen tight collars, ties, and belts to aid respiration
Turn onto side (recovery position) if vomiting or not waking within 1 minute
dont: Never force an unconscious person to drink water or eat sugar
Never make a fainting person stand up quickly

myths.statement: Splashing cold water into a fainted person's face will wake them up safely.
myths.truth: Splashing water can cause aspiration into the windpipe and choke an unconscious person.

quiz.q: A student collapses and faints during morning school assembly. What is the correct response?
options: Lay flat on back and elevate feet 30 cm
quiz.explanation: Laying flat and raising legs restores blood circulation to the brain.

situations: During school assembly at {at}, a classmate suddenly sways and collapses unconscious onto the floor.
scenario.question: What is the proper first aid response for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Lay them flat on their back and elevate their feet/legs
rubric.note: Promotes venous blood return to brain.

rubric.point: Loosen tight collar, tie, and ask crowd to step back for fresh air
rubric.note: Ensures open airway and cool environment.

rubric.point: Do not force liquids into mouth; call school nurse/doctor

sources.name: World Health Organization Basic First Aid

cards.title: Treating sprains and strains with the RICE method
facts: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament supporting a joint (commonly ankle or wrist).
Applying direct ice without a cloth barrier can cause frostbite skin burns.
do: Rest the injured joint immediately—stop playing sports
Ice the area using a cloth-wrapped cold pack for 15-20 minutes
Compress lightly with an elastic crepe bandage and Elevate above heart level
dont: Never apply hot balms, heat packs or massage during the first 48 hours
Never wrap an elastic bandage so tightly that toes turn blue or numb

myths.statement: Massaging a freshly sprained ankle with warm mustard oil speeds recovery.
myths.truth: Heat and massage increase internal bleeding and joint swelling. Use cold RICE protocol.

quiz.q: What does the 'I' in the RICE sprain treatment stand for?
quiz.explanation: Ice constricts injured blood vessels, reducing swelling and pain.

situations: During a basketball match at {at}, {name}'s friend twists their ankle and falls in pain.
scenario.question: How should {name} assist using RICE?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stop play and rest the injured ankle completely
Apply a cold ice pack wrapped in a towel for 15 minutes
Elevate the ankle on a chair/pillow and seek adult evaluation
rubric.note: Facilitates fluid drainage away from joint.

cards.title: Suspected bone fracture: Splinting and immobilization
facts: Moving broken bone fragments can sever adjacent nerves, arteries, and muscle tissue.
Supporting the joint above and below the injury stabilizes the fracture.
do: Keep the injured limb completely still in the position found
Support the limb with rolled magazines, cardboard, or a folded towel as a temporary splint
Call 108 / 112 or get adult transport to an emergency hospital
dont: Never attempt to straighten a bent or deformed limb
Never give food or water in case emergency surgery is needed

myths.statement: If a broken bone looks bent, you should pull it straight right away.
myths.truth: Attempting to realign bones without anesthesia causes severe agony and tears blood vessels.

quiz.q: What is the most critical first aid rule for a suspected broken arm?
options: Immobilize and support it without moving the bone
quiz.explanation: Immobilization prevents bone ends from cutting internal nerves and arteries.

situations: A student falls from the jungle gym at {at} and holds a visibly deformed, painful forearm.
scenario.question: What first aid should {name} provide?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do not move or attempt to straighten the injured arm
Support the limb gently with a sling or soft padding
Call the school nurse/108 and keep the student calm

sources.name: St John Ambulance First Aid Guidelines

cards.title: Snake bite do's and don'ts: Safe emergency response
facts: India's 'Big Four' venomous snakes are the Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper, cobra, and krait.
Cutting, sucking venom, or tying tight tourniquets causes gangrene and limb amputations.
do: Keep the victim calm, still, and reassure them (panic accelerates venom circulation)
Immobilize the bitten limb with a loose splint below heart level
Transport immediately to a government hospital equipped with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV)
dont: Never cut the bite with blades or suck out venom with mouth
Never tie tight rope tourniquets that stop pulse

myths.statement: Sucking venom out with your mouth like in movies saves snake bite victims.
myths.truth: Mouth suction removes zero venom, poisons the rescuer, and introduces deadly mouth bacteria.

quiz.q: What is the only proven medical cure for a venomous snake bite?
options: Anti-Snake Venom (ASV) administered at a hospital
quiz.explanation: Anti-Snake Venom neutralizes circulating venom toxins effectively.

situations: While walking in garden bushes at {at}, {name}'s friend is bitten on the ankle by a snake.
scenario.question: What must {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Keep friend completely calm and still without walking
rubric.note: Muscle contraction pumps venom through lymphatics.

rubric.point: Do not cut, suck venom, or tie tight tourniquets
Rush directly to the nearest hospital with Anti-Snake Venom

cards.title: Bee, wasp and hornet stings: Safe stinger removal
facts: A honeybee stinger has an attached venom sac that continues pumping venom for 60 seconds.
Squeezing a stinger with tweezers or fingers squeezes remaining venom into the skin.
do: Scrape the stinger out sideways using a fingernail or plastic card edge immediately
Wash the area with soap and water, then apply a cold ice pack for 10 minutes
Watch for allergic reactions (facial swelling, throat tightness, breathing trouble) -> 108
dont: Never squeeze the venom sac with tweezers
Never scratch the sting site

myths.statement: Pulling a bee stinger out with pinchers is the best way to remove it.
myths.truth: Pinching squeezes the venom sac like a dropper. Scrape it off sideways.

quiz.q: How should you remove a bee stinger embedded in your arm?
options: Scrape it out sideways with a fingernail or plastic card
quiz.explanation: Scraping removes the stinger without injecting venom from the attached gland.

situations: A bee stings {name}'s classmate on the hand in the garden at {at}.
scenario.question: What is the correct first aid technique?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Scrape the stinger off sideways using a ruler, card or fingernail
rubric.note: Prevents injecting remaining venom sac contents.

rubric.point: Apply a cold ice pack wrapped in a cloth to soothe swelling
Check for signs of severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)

cards.title: Supporting a classmate having an asthma attack
facts: Asthma causes airway narrowing, wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath.
Laying an asthma patient flat makes breathing significantly harder.
do: Help the student sit upright comfortably and stay calm and reassuring
Help them locate their prescribed rescue inhaler (blue cap) and spacer
Call the school nurse or 108 if symptoms worsen or inhaler is unavailable
dont: Never force an asthmatic person to lie down flat
Never crowd around them or give random medicines

myths.statement: During an asthma attack, making the person lie down flat helps them breathe.
myths.truth: Lying down compresses lung capacity. Sitting upright allows diaphragm expansion.

quiz.q: What position helps a student breathe easiest during an asthma attack?
quiz.explanation: Sitting upright with shoulders relaxed gives lungs the maximum expansion volume.

situations: After running in sports class at {at}, a classmate begins wheezing heavily and gasping for air.
scenario.question: How should {name} assist them?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Help them sit upright comfortably and stay calm
rubric.note: Opens airways and prevents panic hyperventilation.

rubric.point: Help them locate their prescribed inhaler with adult supervision
Call the school nurse or teacher immediately

cards.title: Electric shock rescue: Safety of the rescuer first
facts: The human body is an excellent electrical conductor; touching a victim passes current to you.
Electric current causes muscle spasm (tetany), preventing victims from releasing live wires.
do: Turn off the main electrical circuit breaker / switch immediately
If mains cannot be reached, use a dry non-conductive object (wooden broom handle) to separate wire from victim
Check breathing once separated; call 108 / 112 immediately
dont: Never touch an electrocuted person with bare hands while they are connected
Never use metal, wet wood, or damp cloth to push wires away

myths.statement: If someone is caught by electric current, pulling their shirt with bare hands is safe.
myths.truth: Electric current instantly travels through clothing moisture into the rescuer.

quiz.q: What must you do first before touching someone who is touching a live electrical wire?
options: Turn off the main power switch or circuit breaker
quiz.explanation: Always de-energize the circuit first so the rescuer does not get electrocuted.

situations: In the laundry area at {at}, {name} sees someone shaking and frozen touching a frayed appliance cord.
scenario.question: What is {name}'s immediate action?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT touch the victim with bare hands
rubric.keys: do not touch|don'?t touch bare|hands off

rubric.point: Switch off the main power switch or unplug the appliance
Use dry wooden broom handle if switch is inaccessible, then call 108

cards.title: Eye first aid: Chemical splashes and foreign particles
facts: Rubbing an eye with a speck of dust scratches the sensitive transparent cornea.
Chemical splashes (detergents, lab acids, lime) require immediate 15-minute continuous flushing.
do: Flush the eye gently with clean running tap water or saline for 15 minutes for chemicals
Blink repeatedly in a bowl of clean water to dislodge loose eyelashes or dust
Cover loosely with a clean paper cup or eye pad and see an ophthalmologist
dont: Never rub the eye with fingers, knuckles, or dirty handkerchiefs
Never attempt to remove an object embedded into the eyeball with needles or tweezers

myths.statement: Rubbing your eye vigorously removes dust particles quickly.
myths.truth: Rubbing grinds abrasive particles into the corneal lens, causing permanent scarring.

quiz.q: What is the first aid for household cleaning liquid splashed into a student's eye?
options: Rinse immediately with clean lukewarm running water for 15 minutes
quiz.explanation: Continuous irrigation flushes chemicals out before chemical burns occur.

situations: In the chemistry lab at {at}, liquid cleaning detergent splashes into {name}'s classmate's eye.
scenario.question: What must {name} and classmate do immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Rinse eye continuously under running tap water for at least 15 minutes
rubric.note: Flushes chemical irritant before corneal burning.

rubric.point: Do not rub the eye with hands or cloth
Inform teacher and consult an eye doctor immediately

cards.title: Head bump, concussion signs, and danger symptoms
facts: A concussion is a traumatic brain injury that affects mental cognitive function.
Repeated vomiting, confusion, or unequal pupils indicate increasing intracranial pressure.
do: Rest quietly and apply a cold compress wrapped in cloth to the bump for 15 minutes
Monitor closely for red-flag symptoms: repeated vomiting, drowsiness, uneven pupils, confusion
Take to an emergency doctor immediately if red flags appear or if knocked unconscious
dont: Never let an athlete return to play sports on the same day after a head blow
Never ignore a child who cannot remember what happened before the fall

myths.statement: A child who bumps their head can return to playing cricket immediately if they don't bleed.
myths.truth: Concussions occur without external bleeding. Rest and monitoring are vital.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a dangerous symptom following a head bump?
quiz.explanation: Repeated vomiting and drowsiness signal internal brain swelling or bleeding.

situations: During PE class at {at}, a classmate collides heads with another player and falls to the ground dizzy.
scenario.question: How should {name} and the coach manage this head injury?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stop playing immediately and rest quietly
Apply a cold compress to the site of impact
Watch for danger signs: vomiting, severe headache, confusion -> hospital

cards.title: Seizure first aid: Protecting without restraining
facts: Seizures are temporary electrical disturbances in the brain causing involuntary muscle convulsions.
Putting objects into a seizing person's mouth breaks teeth and blocks their airway.
do: Clear hard, sharp, or hot objects away from around the seizing person
Cushion their head with a folded jacket or soft pillow
Turn onto side (recovery position) once jerking stops to keep airway clear
dont: Never put spoons, keys, fingers or cloth into their mouth (they cannot swallow their tongue)
Never hold down or forcefully restrain seizing arms and legs

myths.statement: Putting an iron key in a person's hand stops an epileptic seizure.
myths.truth: Metal keys have zero medical effect on neurological seizures. Keep safe and clear space.

quiz.q: What is the single most important 'DON'T' during an active epileptic seizure?
options: Never force spoons, fingers or keys into their mouth
quiz.explanation: Forcing objects into the mouth breaks teeth and suffocates the person.

situations: A student in the classroom at {at} collapses and begins experiencing jerking convulsions.
scenario.question: What first aid should {name} provide?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Clear nearby desks, chairs, and sharp items away
rubric.note: Prevents head and bodily impact injuries.

rubric.point: Cushion head with folded clothes and do NOT put anything in mouth
rubric.keys: cushion head|nothing in mouth|no spoon|no key

rubric.point: Time the seizure duration and turn to side after jerking stops
rubric.note: Monitors status and prevents saliva aspiration.

cards.title: Water rescue safety: Reach or throw, don't jump in
facts: A drowning person panics instinctively and will climb on top of a rescuer, drowning both.
Over 70% of drowning victims drown within 10 meters of a safe bank or pool edge.
do: Shout loudly for adult help immediately
Extend a long stick, tree branch, bamboo pole, or towel while lying flat on the bank (REACH)
Throw a floating lifebuoy, plastic can, football, or rope (THROW)
dont: Never jump into deep water to rescue someone unless trained in life-saving
Never stand upright on slippery banks while pulling someone

myths.statement: Jumping into the water is the fastest and best way to save a drowning friend.
myths.truth: Untrained rescuers are pulled under and drowned by panicked drowning victims.

quiz.q: What is the golden sequence for non-swimmer water rescue?
options: Shout for help, Reach with pole, or Throw floating object
quiz.explanation: Reach or Throw keeps the rescuer safely dry on the bank while saving the victim.

situations: While near a river bank or pool at {at}, {name} sees someone struggling and splashing in deep water.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Shout loudly for adult help and emergency assistance
Reach with a long stick or branch while lying flat on stomach
rubric.note: Lying flat prevents rescuer being pulled into water.

rubric.point: Throw a floating object (can, tire tube, ring, football)

cards.title: Accidental chemical or pesticide ingestion first aid
facts: Swallowed corrosives (toilet cleaner, acid, bleach) burn the throat coming down.
Inducing vomiting burns the esophagus a second time and can enter lungs (chemical pneumonitis).
do: Call 108 / 112 or national poison control helpline immediately
Identify the substance and keep the bottle/package for doctors
Rinse mouth with water if corrosive was held in mouth without swallowing
dont: Never make the victim vomit (unless specifically told by a poison doctor)
Never force them to drink raw eggs, salt water, or milk blindly

myths.statement: Making a person drink concentrated salt water to induce vomiting is standard poison first aid.
myths.truth: Salt water causes fatal salt poisoning and vomiting burns the esophagus.

quiz.q: If a child accidentally swallows toilet cleaner, why should you NOT induce vomiting?
options: The corrosive chemical burns the throat a second time on the way up
quiz.explanation: Corrosives burn tissue twice if vomited, causing catastrophic airway damage.

situations: A young child at {at} accidentally sips from an unmarked bottle containing liquid floor disinfectant.
scenario.question: What must {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT induce vomiting or force liquids
rubric.note: Prevents chemical burns and lung aspiration.
rubric.keys: do not induce vomiting|don'?t make vomit|no salt water

rubric.point: Keep the chemical bottle and packaging to show emergency doctors
rubric.note: Enables doctors to identify exact toxins.

rubric.point: Call 108 / 112 and rush to hospital emergency immediately

sources.name: National Poisons Information Centre (AIIMS New Delhi)

cards.title: Mastering medical emergency calls (108 / 112)
facts: Emergency dispatchers initiate ambulance sirens while still on the call gathering facts.
Answering dispatcher questions does NOT delay the ambulance arrival time.
do: State exact location first with specific nearby landmark (school gate, petrol pump, temple)
Describe what happened, how many are injured, and if anyone is unconscious
Follow dispatcher instructions and do not hang up until they tell you to
dont: Never hang up in frustration while answering operator questions
Never make prank calls to 108 / 112 (punishable by law)

myths.statement: Staying on the phone answering 108 questions delays the ambulance from leaving.
myths.truth: The nearest ambulance is dispatched immediately; the call gathers preparation data.

quiz.q: Why is stating a prominent landmark essential when calling 108 for an ambulance in India?
options: GPS can be imprecise; landmarks guide drivers directly through crowded streets
quiz.explanation: Landmarks prevent ambulances from getting lost in winding Indian colony streets.

situations: An elderly neighbour collapses at {at} and {name} dials 108.
scenario.question: How should {name} deliver the emergency report?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Give exact colony address, gate number, and nearest landmark first
State patient's consciousness, breathing status, and age
Stay on the line and unlock the building gate for ambulance crew
rubric.keys: stay on line|open gate|wait for crew

cards.title: Assembling a student home first-aid kit
facts: A well-organized first aid kit contains supplies for bleeding, burns, and sprains.
First aid kits should NEVER contain unprescribed prescription medicines or antibiotics.
do: Stock sterile gauze pads, adhesive bandages (band-aids), and medical adhesive tape
Include antiseptic liquid/ointment, blunt-ended safety scissors, and crepe roller bandages
Keep kit in an accessible, dry, cool place known to all family members
dont: Never store loose, expired or unlabeled medicine tablets in a first aid kit
Never lock the kit so tightly that it cannot be opened in a rush

myths.statement: A good first aid kit should be packed with leftover antibiotic capsules.
myths.truth: First aid kits are for immediate trauma care. Unprescribed antibiotics are dangerous.

quiz.q: Which of the following belongs in a standard home first-aid kit?
options: Sterile gauze, adhesive bandages, antiseptic, and scissors
quiz.explanation: Clean wound dressing supplies and antiseptic are standard first aid essentials.

situations: {name}'s family at {at} is assembling their home first-aid kit.
scenario.question: What essential supplies should {name} ensure are packed in the box?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Pack sterile gauze pads, band-aids, and roller bandages
rubric.note: For managing bleeding and bandaging cuts.

rubric.point: Include antiseptic lotion, adhesive tape, and clean scissors
Store in an easily accessible, dry location known to the family
